description: Two four-stage shift registers, each with its own clock, data and reset, and each stage brought out to a jack.

inputs.text: The level read into that register's first stage on each rising clock edge.
While this is high that register is held clear, every one of its four outputs is at 0V, and clock edges are ignored.
A rising edge shifts that register one place along and reads the level at its DATA jack into the first stage.

outputs.text: The first stage of that register: the level read in on the last clock edge.
The second stage of that register: the level read in two clock edges ago.
The third stage of that register: the level read in three clock edges ago.
The fourth stage of that register: the level read in four clock edges ago, after which it is lost.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
The two registers share nothing; patch the fourth output of one into the data input of the other to make a single eight-stage register.
